author: zhuizi
quote: Over a decade of waiting, and somehow Rockstar still hasn't figured out how to make a character walk through a doorway without feeling like a drunk ****'t get me wrong—Leonida looks incredible. The lighting, the water physics, the sheer density of Vice City at night are genuinely impressive. For the first five hours, just driving around feels like a generational leap. Then you actually have to play the game, and the illusion falls apart **** mission design is stuck in 2013. You have this massive, reactive open world, yet the moment you start a story mission, the game puts you on invisible rails. Step ten feet outside the yellow zone or try to flank an enemy from a slightly different angle, and you get hit with an instant "Mission Failed" screen. There is zero room for **** gunplay is equally frustrating. Without heavy auto-aim, shooting feels stiff and unresponsive, and the cover system constantly snaps you to the wrong wall. Combine that with relentless frame drops in downtown areas—even on high-end hardware—and combat becomes a chore.Worst of all, you can feel the shadow of GTA Online hanging over the entire single-player experience. The in-game economy is artificially grindy, basic customization options are bizarrely limited, and it's obvious that the best content is being held back to sell Shark Cards ****'s a technical showcase wrapped around outdated, rigid gameplay. Wait for a steep sale and a year of patches.
